subject: Stellara demo follow-up: prioritized candidate slate + tradeoffs
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Thompson <aisha@stellara.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@stellara.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-25T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Stellara demo follow-up: prioritized candidate slate + tradeoffs

Hi Aisha / Marco —

Thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and a prioritized slate of candidate models we think map to the uses you showed (patient triage intake + short-form clinical summarization). I focused on tradeoffs you flagged: latency under 400ms p95 for triage, summary coherence for clinical notes, and predictable unit-cost for scaling across multiple clinics.

Top 3 candidate options (prioritized):

1) Redwood-Base-8B (quantized) — Balanced
- Quality: Good for structured triage prompts and short summaries (best-in-class hallucination control on our eval set).
- Latency: Median token latency ~45ms on our Dedicated SKU; p95 for 256-token flows ~320ms with continuous batching.
- Cost: Lowest unit-cost after int8 quantization.
- When to pick: If you want predictable low spend and can accept slightly lower long-form summarization fidelity.

2) OpenLlama-13B-xt (optimized kernels) — Latency-conscious higher quality
- Quality: Stronger on abstraction and longer summaries; fewer truncation artifacts.
- Latency: p95 ~420ms on same config (slightly above your 400ms target for worst-case 256 tokens). We can hit 380ms p95 with a small Dedicated profile bump (extra burst nodes) or a low-latency routing policy.
- Cost: Mid-range; still <1.6x Redwood-Base-8B per-token.
- When to pick: If summary coherence is priority and you can accept a small SLA/throughput trade.

3) Falcon-Med-tuned-7B (specialized) — Quality-focused for clinical contexts
- Quality: Best on clinical terminology and instruction-following on our med prompts.
- Latency: p95 ~480ms on baseline; needs quantization + optimized kernel set to approach 400ms.
- Cost: Highest of the three due to longer runtimes and memory overhead.
- When to pick: If the highest clinical correctness for summaries is non-negotiable and you plan targeted routing (e.g., send only complex cases to this model).

Risks & mitigations:
- Quality regression: we recommend adding a small eval harness with 50 representative clinical prompts (we included a starter prompt pack attached). We'll run daily regression checks and alert when any model drifts beyond your thresholds.
- Latency spikes under burst: use a mixed routing policy — Redwood-Base for baseline traffic, OpenLlama for longer summaries, and Falcon-Med gated by rule. This gives a graceful degradation path.

Next steps (proposed):
- Rafael/Karthik: attach benchmark CSV + prompt set (we'll share shortly).
- Mina: provide a 3-tier cost estimate for Q3 (attached PDF) and proposed rollout cadence (pilot -> canary -> prod).
- Aisha/Marco: pick 1-2 models to pilot and confirm expected daily request volume and latency SLO tradeoffs you can accept.

Attaching: stellara_benchmarks_v1.csv (raw perf), stellara_prompt_pack_v2.txt (starter prompts).

Happy to hop on a 20-min sync if you want to walk through the tradeoffs together.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Thompson <aisha@stellara.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@stellara.com>
Date: 2028-07-25T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stellara demo follow-up: prioritized candidate slate + tradeoffs

+1 on Mina's prioritization. A few technical addenda from infra/ops perspective so the commercial ask is realistic: 

- Batching & KV cache: For triage flows (short prompts, high QPS), enable prefix KV caching on patient intake templates — this typically reduces per-token cost ~18% and lowers p95 by ~30ms. We'll include config snippets in the Drive link.
- Quantization profile: Redwood-Base-8B performs best with per-channel int8; OpenLlama-13B needs a mixed-precision int8/float16 profile to keep hallucination risk low. That accounts for the latency delta.
- Burst planning: If you expect >2x peak bursts (e.g., seasonal clinic spikes), plan a burst policy that allows short-lived fleet autoscale with warm nodes — that keeps p95 stable without committing to a larger reserved pool.

I attached a short table in the benchmark CSV with the kernel configs we used and the sequence lengths. Rafael — can you confirm the hardware SKU assumptions (A100 vs H100) that we should price against?

- Karthik
Lead Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Thompson <aisha@stellara.com>

Date: 2028-07-25T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stellara demo follow-up: prioritized candidate slate + tradeoffs

Thanks Mina & Karthik — this is super helpful.

Quick responses from our side:
- We like the Redwood-Base-8B option for baseline triage (cost-conscious).
- For summaries: leaning toward OpenLlama-13B-xt if we can hit 400ms p95 with the suggested routing; coherence is important for clinicians.
- Volume: currently estimating 70k daily triage calls and ~12k summary requests (average 120 tokens).

Can you: 
1) Confirm cost per 1M tokens for the two models under the recommended quant profiles and burst plan.
2) Confirm p95 numbers if we push to a low-latency routing policy (what does the Dedicated SKU need to look like?).

If those two numbers look reasonable, we can sign up for a 6-week pilot. Also copying Marco who'll coordinate procurement.

- Aisha
Director of Product | Stellara Health
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Stellara demo follow-up: prioritized candidate slate + tradeoffs

Thanks — noted. Rafael and I attached the detailed benchmark CSV and a starter prompt pack. The PDF has a rough commercial estimate for Q3 pilot (three-tier: pilot, canary, prod) with per-1M-token estimates. Quick answers inline: 

1) Cost per 1M tokens (approx, pilot reserved + burst):
- Redwood-Base-8B (int8): $38 / 1M tokens
- OpenLlama-13B-xt (mixed int8/fp16 kernel): $62 / 1M tokens

2) p95 with low-latency routing (Dedicated + warm burst nodes, H100-backed):
- Redwood-Base-8B: ~300–350ms p95 (256-token distribution)
- OpenLlama-13B-xt: ~360–390ms p95 (can tighten to ~370ms with small autoscale headroom)

Next steps:
- Rafael: finalize cost_estimate_stellara_Q3.pdf and confirm exact SKU pricing (A100 vs H100) for Marco/procurement.
- Mina/Karthik: set up pilot onboarding doc + shared Slack channel; propose pilot kickoff week of Aug 12.
- Aisha/Marco: confirm pilot acceptance and send a preferred PO contact.

(Attachments: stellara_benchmarks_v1.csv, stellara_prompt_pack_v2.txt, cost_estimate_stellara_Q3.pdf)

Looking forward — happy to jump on a 20-min call later this week to walk procurement through the SKU options.

Best,
Mina Haddad
